claim: Gotter instructions dated 17 November 1740
finding: Document 192 is dated Berlin, 8 December 1740; it refers to earlier instructions to Borcke. Do not conflate those instructions with Gotter’s commission.

claim: Frederick’s price could only rise; partial cession was unavailable
finding: On 26 December Frederick authorized Gotter to indicate willingness to accept a substantial part rather than all of Silesia. This documents an offer, not sincerity or certainty that agreement would last.

claim: Sardinia joined openly only in 1743
finding: The Swiss National Museum dates the Austrian–Sardinian Convention of Turin to 1 February 1742. Correct the 1743-only claim; the original convention was not opened, so this is secondary corroboration.

claim: Khevenhüller listed as Hofkriegsrat Vice-President in 1740/41
finding: The official history gives that office and cites the 1740 and 1741 court calendars. Appointment month and presence in Vienna on 21 October remain unverified.

claim: Court factions, exact Conference roster, all guarantors’ legal obligations, envoys and courier times
finding: The pass does not establish these from dated records. Preserve as research hypotheses; no categorical legal or personal-motive conclusions.

claim: Mollwitz created the entire coalition from nothing
finding: Document 344 refers to treaty negotiations already underway and a French letter dated 7 April. Victory may have affected commitment, but diplomacy did not begin only after 10 April.

claim: Hungary paid only in men and loyalty, never cash
finding: Act LXIII funds infantry from the country’s tax fund, and section 18 specifies cash contributions by towns in lieu of some mounted obligations. Noble exemption is not national fiscal exemption.

claim: Silesian revenues secured foreign debt transferred by peace
finding: Berlin article IX assigns debt owed to English and Dutch subjects to Prussia, subject to the Dutch settlement provision, while the queen retains debt owed to Brabant creditors. No principal amount verified.

claim: Silesia supplied one tenth of revenue; treasury held 100,000 florins; grants took one to three quarters
finding: No comparable dated fiscal series or cash account checked. Remove exact ratios, balances and fixed lags from the operating rules.

claim: Regional grain-price curves and automatic 1740–41 famine unrest
finding: The pass did not establish local harvest, price or mortality series. Weather background cannot determine a province’s unrest without local evidence.

claim: Occupation affects only next year’s budget; British subsidy never arrives when needed
finding: These absolutes are unsupported design rules. Occupation may interrupt current collections and seize chests; subsidy authorisation, remittance and receipt must be tracked separately. Exact British payment dates and sums remain unverified here.

claim: The winter recovery was achieved by a cheap irregular army instead of the paid army
finding: No cost comparison or force composition sufficient for that claim checked. Retain possible raids and operational successes without that causal verdict.

claim: Hungarian noble tax privileges were reaffirmed
finding: Act VIII protects the estates’ fiscal privileges. It does not show that all inhabitants or all forms of contribution were exempt.

claim: 1741 infantry levy authorised
finding: Act LXIII section 1 specifies 21,622 infantry in six new regiments; sections 1–2 specify funding and limits on replacement obligations. This is authorised establishment, not a verified muster or battlefield strength.

claim: 60,000 Hungarian troops actually provided
finding: Replace the unsourced delivered total with the 21,622 authorised infantry levy, separately from noble and mounted obligations. Actual mobilisation and arrival remain unverified.

claim: Exact homage dates, a delayed coronation delays any claim, fixed robot burden, national loyalty blocs
finding: No uniform constitutional or social rule is justified. Verify each jurisdiction, institution, date and locality; never treat a whole confession or province as one actor.

claim: Catholic status quo protected in ceded Silesia
finding: Berlin article VI protects the Catholic religious status quo alongside Protestant freedom of conscience and constrains sovereign interference. Treaty obligation is not proof of perfect enforcement.

claim: Clerical obligations contributed to Hungarian mobilisation
finding: Act LXIII sections 13–16 specify obligations for named clerical categories, with exemptions and assessment rules. It does not establish papal permission or a monarchy-wide cash total.

claim: The Prague expulsion belongs to the 1741–42 opening
finding: The decree is dated December 1744. It cannot be imported into 1741–42 as an event or proof of actual collaboration.

claim: Papal neutrality, 1742 Protestant declaration, exact Carolina Resolutio effects, Orthodox Frontier privileges
finding: No sufficient dated primary evidence opened for these specific claims. Leave provisional; do not hard-code confessional allegiance or a universal papal position.

claim: 7,000 Austrians versus 100,000 Prussians invading Silesia
finding: KA II counts 7,359 excluding Glatz against at least 26,000–27,000 invaders on Silesian soil in late December. KA I’s 99,446 is the whole Prussian army. The 7,359 includes garrisons and is not one field army.

claim: 1,719 men in October 1740
finding: KA II says one regiment was in Silesia in October, but explicitly takes 1,719 from December strength lists. Do not label it an October return.

claim: Mollwitz force estimates in the official history
finding: KA II p. 229 reconstructs 15,788 Austrians from post-battle returns plus losses; p. 224 gives 21,600 Prussians. Preserve source and estimation status. These totals do not map directly to the demo’s counters.

claim: Austrian casualties imply a universal 29% rout threshold
finding: KA II pp. 245–246 totals 4,551 Austrian personnel losses, including missing and prisoners as well as killed and wounded. Dividing by estimated strength describes one battle; it supplies no universal morale threshold.

claim: Wooden ramrods prove a sustained 3:2 firing ratio
finding: KA I pp. 381–382 describes wooden ramrods and a December 1744 resolution for iron ones. Equipment difference alone establishes neither battlefield sustained rates nor a damage multiplier; universal delivery by that date is not shown.

claim: 1748 Principles document Frederick’s exact 1740 doctrine
finding: The treatise was written in 1748 and circulated in 1753. Use as later reflection, not contemporary evidence that the novice king or every unit already behaved that way.

claim: Demo speed, fire, morale, vision, strength and casualty coefficients
finding: The 1.55 fire and 1.18 strength multipliers, movement speeds, 15-minute/12-phase cap and fog ranges remain game assumptions. No source supports substituting precise new coefficients in this pass.
